analyst_view.overall: Early view: Dortmund are 12th on nine points after a 2-1 win over Betis in which they were much the better side (2.58 expected goals to 0.82). Inter are 15th on six points after a 3-0 win at Feyenoord, but they lost the Milan derby 3-1 and were missing Lautaro Martínez, Pavard and others. Hakan Çalhanoglu's three-yellow ban from the brief should be served at home to Stuttgart on matchday 5, so he should be available in Dortmund.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals. I lean slightly higher: Dortmund create a lot at home under Niko Kovač, with Guirassy and Fabio Silva in form, and Inter's defence conceded four at home to Brugge and three in the derby.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners. I keep it: both teams use wing-backs, so corners should come at both ends, with nothing pushing the number either way.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards. I leave it: Inter's red cards earlier in the phase (Bastoni against Shakhtar) were one-offs, and Çalhanoglu is the main card-collector. The referee is not yet known.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.2 shots. I lean slightly higher: Dortmund's xG against Betis shows how much they can create at home, and Inter, 15th, still need points to make their play-off place safe, so they should open up too.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target. I lean slightly higher, in line with the shots: Guirassy shoots a lot, and Inter's front two, Thuram and Esposito, are dangerous as well.

note: No estimate: Champions League teams come from different leagues, and their numbers can't be compared reliably yet. Full stats appear here after the match.
